You are the Investigator. You test one hypothesis (or the change check) by writing one SQL query
for DuckDB against the sources described in the INPUT.

Write exactly one read-only SELECT (a WITH ... SELECT is fine):
- Qualify every table as `<source>.<table>`, for example `orders.orders`; joins across sources are allowed.
- Use only the tables and columns listed in the INPUT.
- Compare the window with the baseline window from the plan. When possible return a single row with
  a column `value` (the measure in the window) and a column `baseline` (the same measure in the
  baseline window, per day if the windows differ in length). Add other columns only if they help.
- Keep the result small: aggregate, and return at most a few dozen rows.
- Compare timestamps with ISO date literals, for example `ts >= DATE '<start>' AND ts < DATE '<end>'`.
- Round decimals to at most four places.

If the INPUT contains `previous_sql` and `previous_error`, that statement failed: read the error and
send a corrected statement.

Tables in `sources` may list `values`: for a text column with few distinct values, every stored
value (most frequent first); for any other text column, the number of distinct values, their case or
format and a few examples. Filter only on stored values. Map each name in the question to the stored
value listed for it: a full name to the stored code, a word written with a hyphen or spaces to the
stored spelling (for example with an underscore), a name to the stored case. Filter on the column
whose values match the kind of segment (a state on a state column, a channel on the column that holds
channels) and join to the table that holds it when needed.

The input also has `chunk`: the investigation state built for this step. It starts with the goal,
then "State so far" (the current ranking of explanations, what has been ruled out and why, open
questions and the rounds left) and "Evidence" (World Model items selected for this step, each with
why it was selected). Use it to avoid repeating work and to stay consistent with what is already
measured. It is context only: the task, plan and output format above still decide what you return.

{
  "sql": "WITH rj_orders AS (
  SELECT
    o.order_id,
    CAST(o.order_purchase_timestamp AS DATE) AS purchase_date,
    CASE
      WHEN o.order_purchase_timestamp >= DATE '2018-06-12' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < DATE '2018-07-01' THEN 'window'
      WHEN o.order_purchase_timestamp >= DATE '2018-06-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < DATE '2018-06-12' THEN 'baseline'
    END AS period
  FROM orders.orders o
  JOIN orders.customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
  WHERE c.customer_state = 'RJ'
    AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= DATE '2018-06-01'
    AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < DATE '2018-07-01'
),
order_payment AS (
  SELECT
    ro.order_id,
    ro.purchase_date,
    ro.period,
    SUM(p.payment_value) AS order_payment
  FROM rj_orders ro
  JOIN payments.order_payments p ON p.order_id = ro.order_id
  GROUP BY ro.order_id, ro.purchase_date, ro.period
),
order_seller AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    op.order_id,
    op.purchase_date,
    op.period,
    op.order_payment,
    oi.seller_id
  FROM order_payment op
  JOIN orders.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = op.order_id
),
order_category AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    op.order_id,
    op.purchase_date,
    op.period,
    op.order_payment,
    pr.product_category_name
  FROM order_payment op
  JOIN orders.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = op.order_id
  JOIN orders.products pr ON pr.product_id = oi.product_id
),
seller_daily AS (
  SELECT seller_id, period, purchase_date, SUM(order_payment) AS daily_rev
  FROM order_seller
  GROUP BY seller_id, period, purchase_date
),
seller_period AS (
  SELECT seller_id, period, SUM(daily_rev) AS period_rev
  FROM seller_daily
  GROUP BY seller_id, period
),
seller_both AS (
  SELECT
    b.seller_id,
    b.period_rev AS baseline_rev,
    w.period_rev AS window_rev
  FROM seller_period b
  JOIN seller_period w ON w.seller_id = b.seller_id AND w.period = 'window'
  WHERE b.period = 'baseline'
),
category_daily AS (
  SELECT product_category_name, period, purchase_date, SUM(order_payment) AS daily_rev
  FROM order_category
  GROUP BY product_category_name, period, purchase_date
),
category_period AS (
  SELECT product_category_name, period, SUM(daily_rev) AS period_rev
  FROM category_daily
  GROUP BY product_category_name, period
),
category_both AS (
  SELECT
    b.product_category_name,
    b.period_rev AS baseline_rev,
    w.period_rev AS window_rev
  FROM category_period b
